Q: Bulk Loading B+ trees: Top-down and Bottom-up approach A:

The main difference is the direction in which the B+ tree is built.

With the top-down approach, construction starts at the root and works toward the leaf level. As new keys are added, nodes may need to be split and the changes propagated back up the tree. This makes the process similar to regular B+ tree insertion.

With the bottom-up approach, the sorted data is used to build the leaf nodes first. Once the leaves are created, their separator keys are used to build the parent level. The same process is repeated until only the root remains.

For bulk loading, the bottom-up method is generally preferable when the input is already sorted. The leaves can be filled sequentially, and the upper levels can then be constructed directly. This avoids many of the splits and parent updates that would occur with repeated top-down insertions, so it can require fewer I/O operations and be more efficient overall.

Q: How to install GnuPlot on Windows? A:

The simplest way is to use the built-in winget package manager

winget install gnuplot
# Or
winget install -e --id gnuplot.gnuplot

Q: How do I expand the plot margins so that chorddiagram doesn't cut of the labels? A:

I know this post is old but it might still help others, I came across this post while searching to fix the same problem:

Setting margins via circos.par(canvas.xlim = c(-1.3, 1.3), canvas.ylim = c(-1.3, 1.3)) does the trick (adjust values accordingly, obviously).
